land.text: 'The Arvernian territory was attached to Aquitania, which now reached as far as the Loire'; 'the civitas of the Arverni, kept within the limits it had held in the period of independence'

successors.note: After Alesia (September 52) the Arverni 'lost their power of suzerainty' but kept 'a status of civitas libera'; the Arverni page has the territory 'attached to Aquitania' under the Empire, and the Alesia page dates the formal provinces of Gaul to Augustus (27 BC).

capitals.name: Gergovia (Gergovie, near Clermont-Ferrand)
capitals.note: The page calls Gergovia 'the chief oppidum of the Arverni' and lists Gandaillat (first, 3rd c.), Corent (probably Strabo's Nemossos) and Gondole as other oppida; it does not say which was the seat in which decade, so one entry spans the life (confidence 1).

correction.text: 'The Arverni occupied the heart of the Massif Central, a territory centred on the valley of the Allier and the Limagne basin'; 'in the area of the later Auvergne'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Arverni row. The page has no infobox and gives no area; it says the civitas under Rome 'kept within the limits it had held in the period of independence' and 'remained one of the largest in Aquitania', so the later Auvergne (about 27,800 km2 by the gazetteer) stands for the core. The clients (vassal events) lie outside this shape; Strabo's claim that Arvernian authority 'once reached as far as Narbonne and the borders of Massalia' is 'heavily exaggerated' on the page and is not drawn.

region.text: 'The Arverni occupied the heart of the Massif Central, a territory centred on the valley of the Allier and the Limagne basin'; 'in the area of the later Auvergne'

ledger.note: c. 250 BC: the Arverni are established in the Massif Central. The page gives no founding date: they 'first appear in the written record at the end of the 3rd century BC' (207 BC, treating with Hasdrubal) after an entity had 'formed for several generations'; the oppidum of Gandaillat is occupied from the first half of the 3rd century BC. 250 is a placeholder; the page is silent.

ledger.counterpart: Vellavii, Gabali, Cadurci and Eleuteti (Arvernian clients)
ledger.note: 2nd century BC: the Arvernian hegemony. 'Headed by their chiefs Luernius and Bituitus, the Arverni dominated many of the neighbouring peoples'; 'Clients of the Arverni included the Vellavii, Gabali, Cadurci and Eleuteti' (each kept its territory, government and institutions: Goudineau's 'hierarchical confederation'). The page gives neither start year nor places; 200 and the departments are the researcher's bridge (page silent).

region.text: the Rhône valley where the Romans met the Allobroges and Arverni: near Vindalium (Bédarrides) and 'where the Isère river meets the river Rhone near current-day Valence'

ledger.note: 121 BC: Rome meets the Arverni and Allobroges in the Rhône valley. Domitius Ahenobarbus fought them 'near the town of Vindalium, the current French town of Bédarrides'; Fabius Maximus beat Bituitus 'Where the Isère river meets the river Rhone near current-day Valence'.

region.text: the Rhône valley where the Romans met the Allobroges and Arverni: near Vindalium (Bédarrides) and 'where the Isère river meets the river Rhone near current-day Valence'

ledger.note: August 121 BC: Bituitus is crushed at the Isère. 'Battle of the Isère River, August 121 BC, where Quintus Fabius Maximus joined the Roman army' (Allobroges page). The Bituitus page puts the battle in autumn, 'It was estimated that 120,000 of Bituitus's army fell', and has him 'taken prisoner and sent to Rome'. The Arverni page: 'After Bituitus was defeated ... this dominance was reduced to suzerainty over a few neighbouring tribes'.

region.text: Gergovia, 'the chief oppidum of the Arverni', on the plateau beside Clermont-Ferrand

ledger.note: 52 BC: Vercingetorix, an Arvernian, leads the Gallic revolt and 'won a victory over the Roman army at Gergovia, the chief oppidum of the Arverni'. The Alesia page: 'Only the Arverni kept their independence thanks to their victory against Caesar at the Battle of Gergovia.' The page gives no month for Gergovia.

ledger.note: September 52 BC: Alesia ends the revolt. 'Alesia proved to be the end of generalized and organized resistance against Caesar's invasion of Gaul'; 'Vercingetorix was surrendered'. Alesia itself was the oppidum of the Mandubii.

ledger.note: 52 BC: the Arverni are brought under Rome. They 'maintained however a status of civitas libera' (the page), and the territory 'was attached to Aquitania' under Augustus; the roman-republic dossier lists central Gaul from the Loire to the Massif Central as a 52 gain.

ledger.note: September 52 BC: the independent Arverni end with the surrender of Vercingetorix; the civitas lives on inside Roman Gaul.

zones.text: the Rhône valley where the Romans met the Allobroges and Arverni: near Vindalium (Bédarrides) and 'where the Isère river meets the river Rhone near current-day Valence'

wars.outcome: Roman victory under Domitius Ahenobarbus and Fabius Maximus: Bituitus captured, the Allobroges brought under Roman rule, the province of Gallia Narbonensis established; the Arverni 'retained independence after the war' but lost their dominance.
wars.note: Wars named as the Gallia Narbonensis page does (125-121); the Arverni took part only in 121. Bituitus page: Vindalium (Bédarrides) then the Isère-Rhône confluence near Valence in autumn 121; the Allobroges page dates the Isère battle to August 121.

zones.text: Gergovia, 'the chief oppidum of the Arverni', on the plateau beside Clermont-Ferrand

wars.outcome: Gallic victory at Gergovia, then defeat and surrender at Alesia in September 52; the Arverni lost their suzerainty but kept civitas libera status.
wars.note: Alesia page: 'September 52 BC'; no date for Gergovia.

certainty.note: No boundary is given by any page; the territory is the later Auvergne (the Barrington Atlas places the Arverni 'east of the Lemovices and Petrocorii, south of the Bituriges Cubi and Aedui, north of the Ruteni, Cadurci and Vellavii, and west of the Segusiavi and Ambarri').

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria (the eu-03 scope: the Gallic tribal states Rome fought). Everything here is thin by the pages: the Arverni page has no infobox, no area and no founding date (first record 207 BC), and the 'empire' of Luernius and Bituitus is not described territorially (Strabo's reach to Narbonne is called 'heavily exaggerated'). The start year 250, the vassal_start year 200 and the client departments are confidence 1. Counterparts: roman-republic's ledger names 'Arverni and Allobroges' (121) and 'Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)' (58-52) as strings; the matching slugs are arverni, allobroges, helvetii. Aedui, Mandubii, Vellavii, Gabali, Cadurci have no dossier. Wikidata id left null (unreachable, not recalled from memory). Family 'france' is a registry key; the earlier eu-03-x dossiers use 'gallic' (not a key).
